about: Maison Rouge is a cognac line from Maison Hardy, one of the old houses of Cognac. Hardy was founded in 1863 by Anthony Hardy, an English wine and spirits broker who settled in the Charente, took the French name Antoine and chose a young rooster as the house emblem. His descendants carried the house through phylloxera, two world wars and a near-collapse in the 1990s; since 2001 it has belonged to the French group H. Mounier, and Bénédicte Hardy, the fifth generation, remains its face.

Maison Rouge is Hardy’s more approachable range, dressed in a red label with a vineyard farmhouse in place of the rooster and built from eaux-de-vie bought from smaller independent growers. The VS blends 60% Fin Bois and 40% Bon Bois, double-distilled in copper Charentais pot stills and aged three to five years in French oak. The VSOP adds 10% Petite Champagne and spends six to ten years in wood. Aging and blending are done by Hardy in Cognac.

Reviewers find the VS dessert-like on the nose, with apple pie and caramel, then orchard fruit and baking spice on a short finish; the VSOP leans toward vanilla, dried fruit and a little tobacco. Both are built for mixing as much as for sipping, and they are natural fits for the classic cognac cocktails, the Sidecar and the Sazerac.
